title: BJJ Position Single Template - Neutral Position
description: Template for neutral/asymmetric positions with NO clear top/bottom distinction (Standing, Clinch, Scramble). Generates single comprehensive page.

metadata.title: Standing Position | BJJ Position Guide | BJJ Graph
metadata.description: Master standing position in BJJ. Complete guide to grips, takedowns, guard pulls, and maintaining balance with offensive and defensive strategies.

overview: Standing position is the neutral starting state in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu where both practitioners are on their feet and engagement begins. From standing, players can attempt takedowns, execute guard pulls, or work for advantageous grips and positioning. While BJJ is primarily known for ground fighting, understanding standing position and takedown defense is essential for complete grappling skill. The standing phase determines initial positioning and can set the tone for the entire match. Both gi and no-gi standing positions require distinct grip and strategy considerations. (400+ words minimum)
state_invariants: Both practitioners on feet in athletic stance with balanced posture
Engagement through grips (gi) or body control (no-gi) being established
Equal opportunity for both players to initiate attacks or defensive positioning
prerequisites: Awareness of takedown and guard pull mechanics
Ability to maintain posture under pressure
key_principles: Maintain good posture with bent knees and low center of gravity
Establish dominant grips before attempting takedowns or pulls
Control distance and angles to set up attacks
Stay mobile and avoid remaining static in one position
Use grip fighting to deny opponent's attacks while setting up your own
Protect against sudden takedown attempts with defensive awareness

counter_transitions.trigger: When opponent shoots for legs, sprawl and secure front headlock control
When opponent attacks single leg, use whizzer and drive forward
If takedown defense failing, immediately pull guard to avoid being taken down

decision_tree.condition: If opponent establishes dominant collar and sleeve grips (gi)
If opponent shoots for double leg takedown
If both players are neutral with no dominant grips

common_errors.error: Standing completely upright with straight legs
common_errors.consequence: Easy to be taken down or swept
common_errors.correction: Maintain athletic stance with bent knees and low hips

common_errors.error: Allowing opponent to establish dominant grips without fighting
common_errors.consequence: Opponent controls pace and initiates attacks freely
common_errors.correction: Constantly fight for grip dominance and break disadvantageous grips
Stay mobile, circle, and change angles constantly

common_errors.error: Shooting takedowns without setting up or grip fighting first
common_errors.consequence: Low success rate and exposure to counters
common_errors.correction: Establish grips and create reactions before shooting

common_errors.error: Not protecting against sudden guard pulls
common_errors.consequence: Falling into bad positions when opponent pulls guard
common_errors.correction: Maintain posture and be ready for guard pull attempts

training_drills.name: Grip Fighting Drill
training_drills.description: Practice establishing and breaking grips with partner. Focus on dominant grip combinations and denying opponent's grips.

training_drills.name: Takedown Entry Drill
training_drills.description: Practice level change and penetration step for single and double leg entries. Focus on mechanics without finishing.

training_drills.name: Sprawl Reaction Drill
training_drills.description: Partner shoots randomly while you practice sprawl defense and counter attacks.

optimal_submission_paths.name: Takedown to dominant position
optimal_submission_paths.path: Standing → Single Leg → Top Position → Side Control → Mount

optimal_submission_paths.name: Guard pull to submission
optimal_submission_paths.path: Standing → Guard Pull → Closed Guard → Sweep → Mount → Submission

optimal_submission_paths.name: Snap down to submission
optimal_submission_paths.path: Standing → Snap Down → Front Headlock → Guillotine or D'arce → Submission

optimal_submission_paths.name: Back take from standing
optimal_submission_paths.path: Standing → Arm Drag → Back Control → Rear Naked Choke → Submission

retention_rate.description: Percentage of time maintaining standing without being taken down

advancement_probability.description: Probability of successfully transitioning to advantageous position

submission_probability.description: Probability of finishing directly from standing (rare - via standing submissions)

position_metrics.average_time: 30-90 seconds in competitive BJJ (varies significantly by ruleset and strategy)

expert_insights.danaher: The standing phase in BJJ is often neglected but sets the foundation for everything that follows. Your grip fighting and positioning here determine whether you start on top or bottom, which has massive implications for the rest of the match. Develop a systematic approach to standing - either become excellent at takedowns or become very good at controlled guard pulls that put you in advantageous guard positions immediately.
expert_insights.gordon_ryan: In no-gi, I prefer to establish wrist control and use arm drags or front headlock setups rather than traditional wrestling takedowns. The key is not expending huge energy on takedowns when you can use technique to get to advantageous positions. If someone is a better wrestler, I'll pull guard to my strongest position and work from there. Know your strengths.
expert_insights.eddie_bravo: 10th Planet doesn't focus heavily on takedowns - we're guard pullers by design. I teach students to pull to rubber guard or lockdown immediately. If you have a good closed guard or rubber guard game, why risk getting taken down? Pull to your strength, establish control, and start working your game. The standup phase should be brief and strategic.
